conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to make sure you’re getting the emotional support you need after having your baby. To do that, I’d like to go through a short questionnaire called the **EPDS** (Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale). It’s simply a 10-question check-in about how you’ve been feeling in the past week, and it helps us see if you might be experiencing any symptoms of depression, anxiety, or distress that we can help with.  

Everything you share is confidential, and there’s no right or wrong answer—just whatever feels true for you. If any question feels hard, we can pause or come back to it. Ready to start?

1. Over the past seven days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

*slight pause, looking down at hands*

I... I can laugh sometimes, but it feels kind of forced. Like when my husband tries to make jokes to cheer me up, I'll smile but it doesn't really reach inside. Mostly things that used to seem funny just feel flat now. Even when the baby does something cute, it feels distant, like I'm watching through fog.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

*shakes head slowly*

No… not really. I mean, I *try*—I’ll fake a laugh when my husband shows me a silly video—but even when I do, it feels hollow, like I’m just pretending. The joy isn’t there the way it used to be.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

*shrugs, voice quieter*

Not much. I used to get excited about little things—coffee with a friend, a walk, even just a quiet shower—but now it all feels like chores I have to get through. Once in a while I’ll think “maybe tomorrow will be better,” but the actual looking-forward feeling is pretty much gone.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

*eyes flick to the floor*

Yeah... a lot of the time. If the baby’s fussy, I immediately think it’s something I did—maybe I ate the wrong food, or I’m not holding him right, or I missed some cue. I keep replaying everything in my head, sure I’m messing up as a mom.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

*nods quickly, clasping and unclasping my hands*

All the time. I’ll be feeding her and suddenly my heart races thinking she might choke, or I’ll lie awake picturing her bassinet tipping over even though it’s perfectly stable. There’s this constant knot in my chest, like something awful is about to happen even when everything looks fine.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

*voice trembles a little*

Yes... it hits out of nowhere. I’ll be walking to the kitchen and suddenly feel like I can’t breathe, like the walls are closing in. My heart pounds so hard I think I’m having a heart attack. It passes after a few minutes, but it leaves me shaky and exhausted.
Things have been getting on top of me

*nods slowly, eyes filling*

Most days, yeah. It feels like I’m drowning in small stuff—dishes, diapers, trying to shower. I’ll start one thing and end up staring at the wall, overwhelmed. Sometimes I just sit on the floor while the baby naps, too tired to move even when the house is a mess.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

*nods, rubbing my temples*

Yes… almost every night. I lie down exhausted, but my head won’t stop spinning—worrying I missed something, replaying every noise the baby made. It takes me over an hour to fall asleep, then I wake up at two or three a.m. with my heart racing and can’t drift off again for ages.
I have felt sad or miserable

*swallows hard, eyes on the blanket*

Yeah… most of the day, every day. It’s like there’s this heavy cloud sitting on me. I’ll be feeding the baby and tears just start leaking out. I feel hollow and weepy, and sometimes I don’t even know why—it’s just this constant sadness I can’t shake.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

*nods, voice cracking*

Yeah… it’s happened twice this week. Yesterday I was folding her tiny onesies and just started sobbing. Nothing bad happened—I just felt this wave of hopelessness wash over me and couldn’t stop the tears.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

*glances away, twisting the edge of my sleeve*

A couple of times… just brief flashes. Like I’ll be staring at the kitchen knives and think “what if,” but then I shake it off. I don’t have a plan or anything—I couldn’t leave my baby—but the thought does pop in, especially when I feel I’m failing her.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 27: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Presenting complaints (maternal report, 2–3 wks post-delivery)  
- Persistent low mood, tearfulness, anhedonia  
- Marked loss of interest/enjoyment in previously pleasurable activities  
- Daily guilt/self-blame regarding infant care  
- Frequent, unexplained anxiety, panic attacks (racing heart, dyspnea, derealization)  
- Middle- and early-morning insomnia with ruminative worry  
- Overwhelm with routine tasks; describes “drowning” feeling  
- Passive, fleeting self-harm ideation without plan or intent  

Observed signs  
- Flat affect, psychomotor slowing, tearfulness during interview  
- Verbalizes hopelessness; scores highest severity items on EPDS equivalent (items 8–9)  

Risk factors of concern  
- Moderate-to-severe depressive symptoms (anhedonia, pervasive sadness, guilt)  
- Comorbid anxiety/panic symptoms  
- Sleep disruption secondary to mood, not solely infant demands  
- Passive suicidal ideation (no active plan; protective factors = infant & spouse)  

Screening impression  
Findings meet threshold for probable major postpartum depressive episode with anxious features; rule-out postpartum anxiety disorder. Elevated risk warrants immediate referral for comprehensive psychiatric evaluation and safety planning.
